title: Whole-tower adjunct characterization of the specified integral comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\lim_m(A_{E,m})_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}_X=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ and let $\Delta$ be the termwise constant-tower functor [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. For a strict tower complex $T_\bullet$, choose a K-injective tower resolution $j_T:T_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-sp-injective-resolutions], compute $R\lim T_\bullet=\lim J_\bullet$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and put $\epsilon_T=[j_T]^{-1}\circ[\Delta\lim J_\bullet\to J_\bullet]$. Then for every $H\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ the map
$$\Phi_{H,T}:\operatorname{Hom}(H,R\lim T_\bullet)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta H,T_\bullet),\qquad f\longmapsto\epsilon_T\circ\Delta(f)$$
is a bijection, natural in both derived variables and independent of the resolution.
For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $q:P\to K$ be the chosen flat-term K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $P_m=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,m})_Y$, $C_{g,m}=\operatorname{Res}_m g_m^*P_m$, with the actual quotient transitions, and $\theta_{g,m}:g^{-1}P\to C_{g,m}$, $x\mapsto\bar x\otimes1$; these are the objects, coefficient actions and units of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Let $\theta_g^\Delta:\Delta g^{-1}P\to C_{g,\bullet}$ be this strict family and identify the specified cone model of $Lg^*K$ with $R\lim C_{g,\bullet}$ by the normalized Roos comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. The specified comparison $\kappa^g_K$ of that definition is characterized uniquely by
$$\epsilon_{C_g}\circ\Delta(\kappa^g_K)=\theta_g^\Delta\circ\Delta[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}.$$
In particular the zero shifted-product cone lift $z\mapsto(0,(\theta_{g,m}(z))_m)$, conjugated by $[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$ and by the normalized Roos identification, is the morphism with this entire-tower adjunct.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$. The sectionwise description of inverse limit gives an additive adjunction $\Delta:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:\lim$: a map $H\to\lim T$ is exactly a family $f_n:H\to T_n$ with $t_nf_{n+1}=f_n$, and the inverse sends the family to its unique limit lift. The ordinary counit $e_T:\Delta\lim T\to T$ is the family of limit projections. Exactness in $\mathcal B$ is levelwise, so $\Delta$ is exact: applying it to a short exact sequence repeats that same short exact sequence at every level. Consequently the termwise $\Delta$ preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits: inverse limit and constant-system inverse image; ordinary adjunction by the limit universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to the additive adjunction of Step 1. It gives $\Delta\dashv\lim$ on homotopy categories with the same termwise counit $e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], total $R\lim$ is defined on all of $D(\mathcal B)$ and its value at $T$ is represented by $\lim J$ for the chosen $j:T\to J$. Since $\Delta$ already inverts quasi-isomorphisms, its left derived functor is $\Delta$ itself: every map in the diagram defining $L\Delta(H)$ is an isomorphism after localization, and the identity representative has value $\Delta H$. Now use [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with its $\mathcal A=\mathcal B$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal A$, $F=\lim$, $G=\Delta$, $K=T$, and $M=H$. This gives a canonical bijection $e_{H,T}:\operatorname{Hom}(H,R\lim T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta H,T)$, functorial in both derived variables. Both categories are abelian, the site is small in the fixed module universe, and the cited tower theorem applies to the sheaf of commutative rings $R_X$; neither boundedness nor exactness of products is needed here.

source.place: Tags 0FND and 0DVC, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general and lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors; sites-cohomology Tag 0941 for the chosen derived-limit model

proof.text: Determine this canonical bijection at $H=R\lim T=[\lim J]$. In the fraction formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], take $s=j:T\to J$, $t=\mathrm{id}_{\lim J}$, and $f=\mathrm{id}_{\lim J}$. The representing map $p_j:[\lim J]\to R\lim T$ is the identity in the chosen model, and the left-derived comparison $u_t$ is the identity because $L\Delta=\Delta$. The ordinary transpose of $f$ is $e_J$. Thus $e_{R\lim T,T}(\mathrm{id})=[j]^{-1}[e_J]=\epsilon_T$. Naturality in the first variable, applied to any derived morphism $h:H\to R\lim T$, gives $e_{H,T}(h)=\epsilon_T\circ\Delta(h)$. This is exactly $\Phi_{H,T}$. The cited canonical bijection is functorial in both localized variables for their representing cocones; changing $J$ changes only the chosen representative of $R\lim T$, so the formula is independent of the resolution under the canonical derived-functor comparison. In particular this establishes naturality for arbitrary derived tower morphisms, not merely levelwise maps.

source.place: Tag 0DVC via 0FND: canonical fraction formula and functoriality in both variables

proof.text: For the integral comparison put $V=g^{-1}P$ and $C=C_{g,\bullet}$. Definition [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b) supplies the actual $R_X$-linear chain maps $\theta_m:V\to C_m$, with $t_m\theta_{m+1}=\theta_m$, hence the strict map $\theta^\Delta:\Delta V\to C$. It also supplies that $g^{-1}(q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and that the specified $\kappa$ is $[\widetilde\theta]\circ[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$, where $\widetilde\theta(z)=(0,(\theta_m(z))_m)$. Countable products in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], including for the completed coefficient sheaf $R_X$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] hold and its normalized isomorphism $\rho_C:\mathsf C(C)\to R\lim C$ identifies this specified cone model with the total derived limit.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; the specified comparison definition (b), normalized Roos comparison, and Bhatt-Scholze exact-product input

proof.text:
Choose $j:C\to J$ as in the normalized Roos comparison. The strict map $j\theta^\Delta:\Delta V\to J$ has an ordinary limit lift $a:V\to\lim J$, characterized by $e_J\circ\Delta a=j\theta^\Delta$. Write $i_J:\lim J\to\mathsf C(J)$ for the inclusion with zero shifted-product component. On the two cone coordinates one has the equality of chain maps $\mathsf C(j)\widetilde\theta=i_Ja$: both send $z$ to $(0,(j_m\theta_m(z))_m)$. The normalization of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] is $\rho_C=[i_J]^{-1}[\mathsf C(j)]$. Therefore $\rho_C[\widetilde\theta]=[a]$. In the derived tower category this gives
$$\epsilon_C\circ\Delta(\rho_C[\widetilde\theta])=[j]^{-1}[e_J]\Delta[a]=[j]^{-1}[j\theta^\Delta]=[\theta^\Delta].$$
This computation is an equality of whole tower morphisms; it does not infer equality from separate projections in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok: comparison via the inclusion of the ordinary inverse limit; normalized strict Roos refinement

proof.text:
Conjugate the equality of Step 5 by the quasi-isomorphism $g^{-1}(q)$ supplied by [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Functoriality of $\Delta$ gives
$$\epsilon_C\circ\Delta\bigl(\rho_C[\widetilde\theta]\,[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}\bigr)=[\theta^\Delta]\circ\Delta[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}.$$
By that definition the map inside $\Delta$ is the specified $\kappa^g_K$ after the prescribed Roos identification. The bijectivity already proved in Steps 2--3, with $H=g^{-1}K$ and $T=C$, says that exactly one morphism has this adjunct. This proves the asserted characterization and its zero shifted-product cone description. The argument applies in the ambient unbounded module derived category and hence to the stated bounded constructible $K$ without adding a hypothesis.
